sbh4.2:1.1: The gross-characteristic in all these lower planes — up through the *ākiñcanyāyatana* — is, in summary, twofold:
sbh4.2:1.2: greater suffering-character of the lower-and-lower planes, and non-calm-abiding-character,
sbh4.2:1.5: He investigates by the six investigation-subjects, as appropriate.
sbh4.2:1.6: For whichever plane he wishes to make dispassion toward, the calm-characteristic is the plane above it, as appropriate —
sbh4.2:1.7: up through the practice-culminating-fruit attention. Then he is 'secluded from sense-pleasures,' or at higher levels, secluded from the analogous gross-content.
sbh4.2:2.1: [At the 1st→2nd transition:] Turning the mind away from the *savitarka-savicāra* objects,
sbh4.2:2.4: in the non-distractedly-moving object, by single-dharma-character, calm, settled, the mind proceeds.
sbh4.2:2.6: Therefore: 'By the calming of *vitarka* and *vicāra*, by inward-confidence' — by the practice of *avitarka-avicāra-samādhi*, transcending the with-cleft, with-interval state, he attains the without-cleft, without-interval state.
sbh4.2:2.7: Therefore: 'By one-pointedness of mind' — by completely abandoning *vitarka-vicāra* in every way, the *avitarka-avicāra* practice-culminating attention is the *samādhi*. Immediately following, conditioned by it, the next arises.
sbh4.2:2.8: Therefore: 'Born from concentration' — from the attainment of the wished-for, undeplored object, or from seeing the fault in *prīti* coming next.
sbh4.2:2.9: Pacifying gone-to-elation and gone-to-dejection, by the disappearance of all the obstructions belonging to the *vitarka-vicāra*-first-*dhyāna*-defilement side, the counter-action of which is *praśrabdhi*, the workableness of mind-and-body —
sbh4.2:2.10: 'Rapture-and-happiness' — by the same understanding as before. By progression, the second comes to be. Everything else as before.
sbh4.2:3.1: He sees the fault in the rapture-signs.
sbh4.2:3.3: At that time, he has attained two mind-disturbance-makers, two obstructions:
sbh4.2:3.4: in the rapture-less third *dhyāna*, settling the mind,
sbh4.2:3.5: and in the second *dhyāna* there were *vitarka-vicāra*; here it is rapture. Therefore: 'He abides in equanimity.'
sbh4.2:3.9: by which without-interval equanimity does not proceed.
sbh4.2:3.10: In the second *dhyāna* there is rapture,
sbh4.2:3.11: by which here too without-interval equanimity does not proceed.
sbh4.2:3.12: Therefore in this contemplator, in the first and second *dhyāna*s, equanimity is not yet; for which reason in the third *dhyāna* 'he abides in equanimity' is said.
sbh4.2:3.13: He, abiding in equanimity, abides thus with mindfulness established.
sbh4.2:3.15: if, due to non-cultivation of the third *dhyāna*, by lapse-of-mindfulness, occasionally perception-and-attention conjoined-with-rapture occur in the mind —
sbh4.2:3.16: those, those, lightly, lightly indeed, by wisdom he penetrates.
sbh4.2:3.18: As they arise, arise, he does not endorse them.
sbh4.2:3.20: pushes out; equanimously regards the mind.
sbh4.2:4.1: By that equanimity, by frequent practice, the rapture-conjoined factors are abandoned.
sbh4.2:4.2: The mind-agitating-maker — the rapture-less, calm, fully-calmed equanimity — arises in the heart, as known.
sbh4.2:4.3: By counter-action to rapture, at that time, in the form-body and the mind-body, happiness and *praśrabdhi*-happiness are experienced.
sbh4.2:4.5: that form-happiness does not exist; nor does without-interval equanimity. From the third *dhyāna* upward, although equanimity is found,
sbh4.2:4.7: Below, sense-pleasure-equanimity is absent; above, happiness is absent.
sbh4.2:4.8: This is that base — the third *dhyāna* — which the noble ones declare.
sbh4.2:4.9: In dependence on this, the attaining-and-abiding person who is mindful and the happy-abider attains and abides in the third *dhyāna* — so the noble ones, the elders, the elder disciples say.
sbh4.2:5.1: Among the noble, there is no equality of category.
sbh4.2:5.2: Of the antidote to *sukha*, the abandonment-antidote is unannounced.
sbh4.2:5.3: What is, by counter-action to that, *sukha-prahāṇa* — that is announced.
sbh4.2:5.6: By practicing this, dropping out from the third *dhyāna*, where there is third-*dhyāna*-plane *sukha*, that he abandons.
sbh4.2:5.7: Therefore: 'By abandoning *sukha*, and previously by abandoning *duḥkha*, by the disappearance of *saumanasya* and *daurmanasya*.'
sbh4.2:5.8: In the fourth-*dhyāna*-attainment-time, that contemplator attains the transcendence of pleasure-and-pain.
sbh4.2:5.9: Of what was previously abandoned, of what is now abandoned,
sbh4.2:5.11: 'From the abandoning of pleasure, from the abandoning of pain, from the previous disappearance of joy and dejection.'
sbh4.2:5.12: Not in the fourth-*dhyāna*-attainment-time alone is *sukha* abandoned; in second-*dhyāna*-attainment-time *duḥkha* is; in third-*dhyāna*-attainment-time *saumanasya* sets; in first-*dhyāna*-attainment-time *daurmanasya* is set. There is at least, by the abandoning of pleasure-and-pain, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling for him; not specially-marked.
sbh4.2:5.13: Therefore: 'Neither-painful-nor-pleasant' — at that time, taking the first *dhyāna* as the starting reference, all the lower-plane defilements are abandoned.
sbh4.2:5.15: By the abandoning of these, the equanimity there arising,
sbh4.2:5.16: and the mindfulness — that becomes purified,
sbh4.2:5.17: fully clarified. By which his mind, having attained the fourth *dhyāna*, stands without movement —
sbh4.2:6.1: Of one whose mind is resolved on space, the form-perception — connected with blue-yellow-red-white etc. — is transcended by indifference-toward and dispassion-toward.
sbh4.2:6.2: Therefore: 'From the transcendence of form-perceptions' — for the cause of the mind proceeding to the limit. The obstruction-perceptions of various kinds, many-and-varied, caused by the accumulation-of-color, those go away.
sbh4.2:6.3: Therefore: 'From the disappearance of obstruction-perceptions.' Or, by the cause-of-disappearance of those, the abundance-perception proceeding in the remaining superior aggregations — namely, perceptions of food, drink, clothing, ornaments, house, garden, forest, army, mountain, etc.
sbh4.2:6.4: — in those, all and every directed-effort no longer proceeds.
sbh4.2:6.6: Having thus cultivated form-obstruction-manifold-perception, he becomes resolved on space by the infinity-aspect.
sbh4.2:6.7: Therefore: 'Infinite space' — taking the immediate-vicinity, transcending — from the practice-culminating attention to the high-practice-culminating-fruit, he attains the basic attainment.
sbh4.2:6.8: Therefore: 'Having attained, he abides in the infinity-of-space-base.'
sbh4.2:7.1: Until the basic attainment is not attained,
sbh4.2:7.2: for the attainer of the space-as-object stage, that and the other aggregates are own-plane; the immediate-vicinity ones are also lower-plane aggregates.
sbh4.2:7.3: By a moment of consciousness, infinite space is resolved-on.
sbh4.2:7.4: That very consciousness, with the infinite-aspect of space-resolve —
sbh4.2:7.7: that very consciousness is resolved-on with the infinite-aspect.
sbh4.2:7.8: With its immediate-vicinity, the basic *ākāśānantyāyatana* is transcended.
sbh4.2:7.10: He, transcending the immediate-vicinity of *vijñānānantyāyatana*, from the practice-culminating attention to the basic-practice-culminating-fruit, attains.
sbh4.2:7.11: Therefore: 'Having attained, he abides in the *vijñānānantyāyatana*.'
sbh4.2:8.1: He, dropping out from the *vijñānānantyāyatana*, searching for an object beyond consciousness, does not find one —
sbh4.2:8.2: neither connected with form, nor formless.
sbh4.2:8.3: Not finding that object, transcending the *vijñānānantyāyatana*-with-its-immediate-vicinity, he resolves: 'There is nothing else as an object.'
sbh4.2:8.4: He becomes resolved on the perception of nothingness.
sbh4.2:8.5: By the abundance of this perception-resolve, transcending the *ākiñcanyāyatana*-immediate-vicinity, from the practice-culminating attention, he attains the basic practice-culminating-fruit.
sbh4.2:8.6: Therefore: 'Transcending the *vijñānānantyāyatana* completely, there is nothing, the *ākiñcanyāyatana* — having attained, he abides.'
sbh4.2:9.1: Therefore: 'Perceiving' — namely, dropping out from the *ākiñcanyāyatana*,
sbh4.2:9.2: gross-perceiving, fault-perceiving the perception-of-nothingness, he turns away the *ākiñcanyāyatana*-perception.
sbh4.2:9.3: By that previous *ākiñcanyāyatana*-attainment-time, the perception-of-nothingness was transcended; now the *non*-perception-of-nothingness has come to be transcended.
sbh4.2:9.4: Therefore: 'Perceiving — namely, perception-of-nothingness or non-perception-of-nothingness or non-perception-of-nothingness.' Not, however, that all and every perception of his is ceased.
sbh4.2:9.5: As in the non-perception-attainment or the cessation-attainment — but here, a subtle perception proceeds, with sign-as-object.
sbh4.2:10.1: There are two non-conscious attainments: the non-perception attainment and the cessation attainment.
sbh4.2:10.2: The non-perception attainment is entered by an ordinary person using perception-turned-away attention; the cessation attainment, however, is entered only by a noble one.
sbh4.2:10.3: By two attentions, entry into these two attainments occurs:
sbh4.2:10.4: namely, into the non-perception attainment by perception-turned-away attention; into the cessation attainment by attention dropping-out from *naivasaṁjñā-nāsaṁjñā* and resolving-on-cessation-of-object.
sbh4.2:11.1: By the basis of *dhyāna*, the projection of the five higher knowledges occurs.
sbh4.2:11.3: Just as the contemplator becomes an attainer
sbh4.2:11.5: Relying on that pure *dhyāna*: whatever dharma he has heard, grasped, fully obtained — bearing on the higher-knowledge-predominant, namely the range-of-supernormal-power, recollection-of-past-abodes, divine-ear, divine-eye, knowledge-of-others'-minds — that very dharma he attends to with concentrated-plane-attention. He becomes meaning-knower
sbh4.2:11.7: Of that meaning-knowing, dharma-knowing practitioner, making the mind so-and-so, by the practice of frequent-cultivation —
sbh4.2:11.8: the time, the moment, becomes when his fruits-of-projection, the five higher knowledges, arise.
